keywords.nuance: まるで often introduces vivid comparison. It usually appears with negative verbs like ない in expressive comparisons.
keywords.exampleTranslation: It feels just like a dream.

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Do not overuse まるで with plain affirmative statements. In many natural patterns it appears before negative forms to express a stronger contrast.

questions.prompt: この景色はまるで絵みたいです。
questions.answer: This view is just like a painting.

questions.prompt: まるで何も起きていないみたいです。
questions.hint: The speaker emphasizes the feel of 'as if nothing happened.'

questions.prompt: 彼はまるで忘れられないです。
questions.hint: This sentence is slightly awkward and needs comparison context.
questions.answer: I can’t forget it at all.

questions.prompt: まるで夢の中にいるようです。
questions.answer: It feels like I am in a dream.

productionQuestions.prompt: The room was so quiet, it was like a library.
productionQuestions.hint: Use まるで for a strong simile.

referenceAnswers.answer: まるで図書館のように静かだった。
referenceAnswers.note: Very natural comparison with 〜のように.

referenceAnswers.answer: まるで図書館みたいに静かだった。

productionQuestions.prompt: He looked so tired, as if he had not slept at all.

referenceAnswers.answer: 彼はまるで眠れなかったみたいに疲れていた。
顔を見ると、まるで徹夜したみたい。
referenceAnswers.note: More spoken and natural to learners.

productionQuestions.prompt: It looked like everyone was surprised for the same reason.
productionQuestions.hint: Use まるで to describe a shared expression.

referenceAnswers.answer: まるで全員が同じ理由で驚いているみたいだった。
referenceAnswers.note: Uses みたい with まるで to emphasize shared reaction.

referenceAnswers.answer: まるで皆、一つの理由で驚いたようだった。

productionQuestions.prompt: The old train station felt like a scene from a movie.

referenceAnswers.answer: その古い駅はまるで映画のワンシーンみたいだった。
referenceAnswers.note: Very natural and concrete image-based expression.

referenceAnswers.answer: まるで映画に出てくるような古い駅だった。
referenceAnswers.note: Keeps cinematic comparison while changing structure.
